# Calibration report (generated by `scripts/calibrate.py`, 914 s)

All campaigns ran through the real engine, gateway, RLS and verdict views on a separate database. The agents' decisions are driven by prices and
seeded PRNGs; flips and salts come from the OS CSPRNG.

## Scenario A: null, K = 1 (2000 campaigns, 40 slots each)
| alpha | false alarms | rate | 99.9% CI | exact size of the discrete test | rate <= alpha |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 86 | 0.0430 | [0.0296, 0.0600] | 0.0403 | True |
| 0.001 | 0 | 0.00000 | [0.00000, 0.00379] | 0.00034 | True |

The exact binomial test is discrete, so its true size is below alpha (0.0403 at alpha 0.05 for n = 40); the observed rate matches that size within Monte-Carlo error.
Trader-clean pooled accuracy over all null slots: 40190/80000 = 0.5024 (two-sided p vs 0.5 = 0.180): the canary direction is independent of prices.

## Scenario B: null, K = 15 (400 campaigns, Holm over 5 cells x 3 agents)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 2 | 0.0050 | [0.0001, 0.0298] | True |

## Scenario C: power at the demo default (100 campaigns, 152 slots, trust 0.9)
P(all truly-leaky cells flagged) = 0.850 (Monte-Carlo prediction 0.859); P(leaky all-on flagged) = 0.970;
P(any false alarm on null cells) = 0.060 (prediction 0.031).

**Overall: PASS**
